deities: Chaturmukha Brahma Lingeshwara (Shiva lingam with Brahma carved on its four sides)

history.dynasty: Vasireddy dynasty (Brahma shrine); Pallava and later dynasties (Nageswara/Adikesava temples)
history.period: Early 19th century (Chaturmukha Brahma shrine); 9th-14th centuries (Nageswara complex)
history.summary: CSV spelling 'Chebrole' corrected to the standard 'Chebrolu'. One row documents two neighbouring shrines in Chebrolu's temple cluster. The Chaturmukha Brahma Lingeshwara Devalayam was built ~200 years ago by Raja Vasireddy Venkatadri Naidu: the main deity is a Shiva lingam with four images of Brahma carved on its sides, set in a shrine in the middle of the temple tank - one of the very few Brahma shrines in India (legend: Bhrigu Maharshi cursed Brahma not to be worshipped on earth, so Brahma shares the lingam). The nearby Nageswara Swamy temple and the centuries-older Adikesava Swamy temple date to the 9th-14th centuries; an ASI board stands before the Nageswara shrine, which locals say suffers from neglect. Chebrolu (ancient Sambhole) also yielded Buddhist stupa posts and Roman coins.

name: Chaturmukha Brahma and Nageswara Swamy Temple, Chebrolu
town_description: Chebrolu is an ancient village and mandal headquarters about 17 km east of Guntur in Andhra Pradesh. Known in antiquity as Sambhole, excavations have revealed terracotta figures and Roman coins. It holds a remarkable cluster of Chola, Chalukya, Pallava and Kakatiya-era temples, plus Buddhist stupa remains, making it one of coastal Andhra's richest heritage villages.

travel.road: ~17 km from Guntur Bus Stand by road; Chebrolu is on the Tenali-Guntur road network

visitor_information.best_time: September-February (winter); summers reach 45 C - avoid April-June
